reviewMethod: Inspected four neutral Cycles 32-sample views and eight rendered phase poses for each clip. Checked every source animation frame for stance-claw ground height, root translation and exact loop endpoint equality. Inspected a fresh raw-GLB reimport render for portable geometry and materials. The source skin audit samples nine poses per clip; the separate Three.js GLTFLoader CPU roundtrip audit compares both optimized variants against source bounds.
notes: Original reference-guided educational model, authored from custom vertex surfaces, not assembled Blender primitives or imported models.
The shell pigment, keratin growth marks, skin cells and relief scales are procedurally authored interpretations, visibly simplified rather than photogrammetric or photoreal scanned detail.
Front, side, rear and three-quarter views show grounded forefeet, tapered forearm shoulders, short broad head, club-like hindlimbs and a projecting yellow-brown plastron.

All four clips are original in-place interpretations, not motion capture or a biomechanical simulation. Walk uses alternating slow stance and lifted recovery; Turn pivots roughly 24 degrees and returns; Dig alternates short forelimb scrapes. These are treadmill-style clips, not world-locked IK locomotion.

Every-frame stance claw height is approximately 0 to 0.76 mm; Idle breathing adds at most 0.50 mm. No visible ground penetration or separated scales/joints was observed in reviewed poses. All root translations are zero and loop endpoint bone matrices match exactly.

Eight glTF inherited skin-transform warnings arise from the common grounding translation. The Three.js GLTFLoader CPU roundtrip audit found no gross grounding/deformation mismatch; warnings are retained transparently.
The legacy gopher-tortoise-qa.png alias has been replaced by the final three-quarter render.

Fresh Blender raw-GLB animation reimport matched source evaluated bounds across nine phases per clip within 0.000000075 m. Four additional reimported Walk/Dig phase renders were inspected without deformation or material defects.

Decoded optimized desktop GLB was reimported into Blender and rendered: geometry, skin and compressed material pixels inspected. Decompression changed no vertex/animation data; WebP pixels were losslessly converted to PNG solely for Blender review. This is not a browser screenshot.
Root also inspected the decoded optimized mobile export in a neutral Blender render: anatomy, pigment and shell/flipper or limb boundaries remain coherent. This is not a browser screenshot.
